--- a/yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py
+++ b/yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py
@@ -5218,12 +5218,17 @@ class _UnsafeExtensionError(Exception):
         'sbv',
     ])
 
+    _enabled = True
+
     def __init__(self, extension, /):
         super().__init__(f'unsafe file extension: {extension!r}')
         self.extension = extension
 
     @classmethod
     def sanitize_extension(cls, extension, /, *, prepend=False, _allowed_exts=()):
+        if not cls._enabled:
+            return extension
+
         if extension is None:

issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))

DO NOT post duplicates
- [x] I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I'm downloading albums that don't have proper track numbers in their metadata, using the playlist autonumbering instead, eg.
`yt-dlp -xvU --parse-metadata playlist_autonumber:track https://www.youtube.com/watch?list=OLAK5uy_kStdcYOA3O0_XR32WmLtXYJDZIEAjiChk`

This always prints `[MetadataParser] Could not interpret 'playlist_autonumber' as 'track'`

Seems to be a one-line fix, though; PR to follow.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

- [x] Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
- [ ] If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead

issue_title: [Announcement] Discontinuing `macos_legacy` builds (ATTN: macOS 10.9-10.14 users)
issue_body:
### `macos_legacy` builds will discontinued at the end of August 2025.

### What Does This Mean?

1. `darwin_legacy_exe` binaries (`yt-dlp_macos_legacy`) will no longer be included with yt-dlp releases.
2. The minimum required macOS version for using the PyInstaller-bundled yt-dlp executables will be bumped from **10.9** to **10.15**.
3. No support will be provided on this tracker for users trying to bundle their own yt-dlp executables on macOS versions older than **10.15**.

### Why?

[**GitHub announced that their `macos-13` GitHub Actions runners will be discontinued beginning in September 2025**](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-11-upcoming-changes-to-macos-hosted-runners-macos-latest-migration-and-xcode-support-policy-updates/#macos-13-is-closing-down).
This is what we are currently using for the `macos_legacy` build jobs. Upgrading to the `macos-14` runner is not viable for the legacy builds, since it runs exclusively on Apple Silicon (ARM64) as opposed to `macos-13`'s Intel x86-64. 

Furthermore, [**PyInstaller officially only supports macOS version 10.15 and above**](https://pyinstaller.org/en/stable/requirements.html#macos). In hindsight, it seems unwise that we were ignoring this and trying to support older versions.

And even if we tried to hack something together that we thought *might* work on macOS <10.15, we have no way of testing it.

### What Do I Need To Do?

The [**`darwin_exe`/`yt-dlp_macos` executable for macOS versions 10.15 and above**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/latest/download/yt-dlp_macos) will continue to be available beyond August 2025. If you wish to migrate to this executable, then you'll need to upgrade your macOS to version 10.15 or newer. Then, if you already have a PyInstaller-bundled executable installed, the next time you update your `darwin_legacy_exe` binary, it will be automatically migrated to `darwin_exe`.

If your system's hardware can't support macOS version 10.15 or newer, then you'll need to use a [Python installation](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Installation#with-pip) or [zip executable](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Installation#installing-the-release-binary) of yt-dlp. Note that your system's Python version must meet yt-dlp's current minimum requirement (which is 3.9 now, but [**will be bumped to 3.10 in October 2025**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13858)).

issue_title: `provide_automatic_options` is weird
issue_body:
While dealing with trying to detect duplicate routes in https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/issues/3105, I ran into an issue with Flask, which adds `OPTIONS` to every single rule by default.

I started looking into Flask's `provide_automatic_options` feature, and it's just weird.

- Why is there a `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` config? What benefit is there to turning `OPTIONS` off at all, let alone configuring it for a given deployment.
- Flask adds `OPTIONS` to every route, then has a check that runs on dispatching _every_ request to see if the method was `OPTIONS` and `provide_automatic_options` was enabled for the rule. Performing this check for every request seems wasteful, as opposed to adding an actual rule and endpoint so that the routing that's already happening handles it.
    - But adding a rule is also sort of bad, as it results in a bunch of duplicate rules since Flask has no way to know what other rules have already been added. This can be caught with Werkzeug 3.2, and doesn't cause problems in earlier versions, but it's still annoying.
- `provide_automatic_options` can be set as an attribute on the view function. There are some other attributes that are barely documented as well, such as `required_methods`. This is presumably mostly for `View` classes, but works on functions too, making type annotations unhelpful.
- If `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` is disabled (not the default), the logic for the `provide_automatic_options` argument and attribute doesn't work correctly to _enable_ it, it only works for _disabling_.
- The tests for this were incomplete and had some issues. Some other tests were revealed to be adding duplicate rules as well. 

At a minimum I've fixed the enabling issue. I've also got a change that registers a route and view for options instead of using special dispatch logic. We should also consider deprecating the config.

     ``GET`` and ``POST`` redirects, and is also correct for frontend libraries
     such as HTMX. :issue:`5895`
+-   ``provide_automatic_options=True`` can be used to enable it for a view when

issue_title: Session is not updated on redirect target endpoint in tests
issue_body:
Hello team.
During writing tests, I noticed a strange session behavior.

I want to verify that after a redirect, the target location sets valid session properties, and it seems like in tests, the session properties when following redirects are not saved/exposed to the test environment.

Here's an example:
```python
import pytest
from flask import Flask, redirect, session

@pytest.fixture
def app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.debug = True
    app.secret_key = 'test_secret'  # noqa: S105 – fake secret key for testing purposes

    @app.get('/redirect')
    def do_redirect():
        print("Redirecting to target endpoint", flush=True)
        session["redirected"] = "true"
        return redirect('/target', 302)

    @app.get('/target')
    def target():
        print("Target endpoint reached", flush=True)
        session['foo'] = 'bar'
        return 'Target', 200

    return app

@pytest.fixture()
def client(app):
    return app.test_client()

def test_session(client):
    with client:
        response = client.get("/redirect", follow_redirects=True)

        print(f"Session after a redirect: {session.items()}", flush=True)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.data == b"Target"

        assert session.get("redirected") == "true"
        assert session.get('foo') == 'bar'

        client.get("/target", follow_redirects=True)
        assert session.get('foo') == 'bar'
        assert response.data == b"Target"
        print(f"Session after a direct request: {session.items()}", flush=True)
```

The test fails on the first assertion `assert session.get('foo') == 'bar'`. 
If I comment it out, the test output is the following:

```
Redirecting to the target endpoint
Target endpoint reached
Session after a redirect: dict_items([('redirected', 'true')])
Target endpoint reached
Session after a direct request: dict_items([('foo', 'bar'), ('redirected', 'true')])
```

**IMPORTANT**: The described behavior is not reproduced when running the application with the real HTTP requests.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.13
- Flask version: 3.10

issue_title: robots.txt enforcement fails OPEN for 2nd+ concurrent same-host request (RobotsTxtMiddleware + Twisted Deferred.asFuture())
issue_body:
## What happened

With `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, a path disallowed by robots.txt was fetched (HTTP 200) instead of being blocked — but only when it was the **2nd or later concurrent request to the same host**. Reproduced 4/4 runs, deterministically.

**Versions:** Scrapy 2.19, Python 3.12 (Twisted as bundled with the Scrapy 2.19 install — exact version available on request).

## Reproduction

1. Serve a local test site (`python -m http.server`) with robots.txt containing:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /private/
```
2. Run a spider with `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, `DOWNLOAD_DELAY=1.0`, `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1`, AutoThrottle enabled, honest User-Agent, requesting three URLs on that host: a live page, a 404, and `/private/x.html`.
3. Observe: `/private/x.html` returns 200 and reaches the parse callback instead of being filtered by the robots middleware.

## Root cause (instrumented)

Concurrent same-host requests share a single Twisted `Deferred` for the robots.txt fetch/parse inside `RobotsTxtMiddleware`. The middleware converts that Deferred per-waiter via `Deferred.asFuture()` — and Twisted's `asFuture()` delivers the real result to the **first** future and **`None`** to the second. The second waiter therefore gets `parser=None`, and `process_request_2` treats `None` as "no parser available → allow the request."

So robots.txt enforcement **silently fails open** for every concurrent same-host request after the first, on the very first robots.txt fetch for a host.

## Expected behavior

All waiters on the shared robots.txt Deferred should receive the parsed result (or all should fail closed — block the request — if the parse result is unavailable).

## Suggested fix directions

- Share the *parsed* result (not the raw Deferred) across waiters; or
- Fail closed: treat `parser=None` as "deny" rather than "allow" in `process_request_2`.

## Workaround

Serialize same-host requests so two requests never race the first robots.txt fetch of a host (e.g. `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1` plus a per-host delay), or pre-fetch robots.txt before crawling.

## Why this matters

Fail-open robots.txt enforcement is a compliance footgun: users who set `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True` believe disallowed paths are never fetched. Under concurrency, that guarantee silently breaks.

---
*Found while building a polite liveness-checker that deliberately serializes per-host requests; the serialization accidentally immunized us, which is how the race was isolated. Happy to provide the minimal spider + test server scripts.*

issue_title: Get rid of get_event_loop()
issue_body:
`asyncio.get_event_loop()` is deprecated and in most cases we should use `get_running_loop()` instead, taking care not to run that code before the loop starts. 

Current uses:
* `AsyncCrawlerRunner._crawl()` - may need further refactoring, maybe together with `Crawler.crawl()`/`Crawler.crawl_async()`, but may require behavior changes in the latter
* `AsyncCrawlerProcess.start()`
* `AsyncioLoopingCall.start()`
* `call_later()`
* `deferred_to_future()`
* `_schedule_coro()`

issue_title: Request.from_curl() incorrectly strips a leading "$" from request data
issue_body:
<!--

Thanks for taking an interest in Scrapy!

If you have a question that starts with "How to...", please see the Scrapy Community page: https://scrapy.org/community/.
The GitHub issue tracker's purpose is to deal with bug reports and feature requests for the project itself.

Keep in mind that by filing an issue, you are expected to comply with Scrapy's Code of Conduct, including treating everyone with respect: https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

The following is a suggested template to structure your issue, you can find more guidelines at https://docs.scrapy.org/en/latest/contributing.html#reporting-bugs

-->

### Description

`Request.from_curl()` incorrectly removes a leading `$` character from
`-d`, `--data`, and `--data-raw` values when `$` is part of the actual
request data.

This silently changes the request body parsed from a valid cURL command.
This is especially problematic for OData-style request bodies, where names
such as `$top`, `$skip`, `$filter`, `$select`, and `$expand` are valid.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the following Python code:

```python
from scrapy import Request

request = Request.from_curl(
    "curl 'http://example.com/' --data-raw '$top=10&$skip=5'"
)

print(request.body)

+def _normalize_curl_command(curl_command: str) -> str:
+    """Normalize Bash ANSI-C quote prefixes for shlex."""
+    result: list[str] = []
+    in_single_quote = False
+    in_double_quote = False
+    escaped = False
+
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(curl_command):
+        char = curl_command[i]
+
+        if escaped:
+            result.append(char)
+            escaped = False
+        elif char == "\\" and not in_single_quote:
+            result.append(char)
+            escaped = True
+        elif char == "'" and not in_double_quote:
+            in_single_quote = not in_single_quote
+            result.append(char)
+        elif char == '"' and not in_single_quote:
+            in_double_quote = not in_double_quote
+            result.append(char)
+        elif (
+            char == "$"
+            and i + 1 < len(curl_command)
+            and curl_command[i + 1] == "'"
+            and not in_single_quote
+            and not in_double_quote
+        ):
+            result.append("'")
+            in_single_quote = True
+            i += 1
+        else:
+            result.append(char)
+
+        i += 1
+
+    return "".join(result)
+

issue_title: Per-domain / per-slot concurrency is not enforced with the asyncio reactor when download delay is 0
issue_body:
## Description

With the asyncio reactor and no download delay, a download slot's concurrency limit is
not enforced.

In the reproduction below, `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN = 2` lets 18
requests to one host run at once; the server confirms it receives all 18 together. A
`DOWNLOAD_SLOTS` entry with `concurrency` and no `delay` behaves the same way, as it
goes through the same code.

Scrapy's own defaults hit this case (asyncio reactor, `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN = 8`,
`DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 0`). With them, the same script reaches up to 15 simultaneous requests
to one host against the limit of 8. The exact peak varies between runs, and
`CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 16` caps how far it can go. Projects generated by `startproject` set
`DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 1`, which hides it.

## Steps to reproduce

Self-contained, no network access needed: it serves its own endpoint on localhost.

```python
"""Minimal reproduction: per-slot concurrency is not enforced when delay is 0.

Serves a local endpoint that holds each response open for HOLD seconds, sends
BURST requests to it with CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN = 2 and no download
delay, and reports the largest number of requests in flight at any one time,
both as Scrapy counts them (the slot) and as the server sees them.

    $ python mre.py                    # asyncio reactor -> peak 18, limit ignored
    $ DELAY=0.05 python mre.py         # non-zero delay  -> peak 2
    $ REACTOR=select python mre.py     # SelectReactor   -> peak 2
"""
import os
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import scrapy
from scrapy.crawler import CrawlerProcess
from twisted.internet.task import LoopingCall

CONCURRENCY = 2
BURST = 20
HOLD = 0.25                                # how long each response is held open
DELAY = float(os.environ.get("DELAY", 0))  # DOWNLOAD_DELAY
REACTOR = {
    "asyncio": "twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor",
    "select": "twisted.internet.selectreactor.SelectReactor",
}[os.environ.get("REACTOR", "asyncio")]


_lock = threading.Lock()
_in_flight = 0
_server_peak = 0


class _Endpoint(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def do_GET(self):
        global _in_flight, _server_peak
        with _lock:
            _in_flight += 1
            _server_peak = max(_server_peak, _in_flight)
        time.sleep(HOLD)
        with _lock:
            _in_flight -= 1
        body = b"ok"
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


_server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _Endpoint)
PORT = _server.server_address[1]
threading.Thread(target=_server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()


class BurstSpider(scrapy.Spider):
    name = "burst"
    custom_settings = {
        # Far above the per-domain limit, so the slot is the only thing that
        # could bound this traffic.
        "CONCURRENT_REQUESTS": 100,
        "CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN": CONCURRENCY,
        "DOWNLOAD_DELAY": DELAY,
        "LOG_LEVEL": "ERROR",
        "TWISTED_REACTOR": REACTOR,
    }

    peak = 0
    started = None

    async def start(self):
        self.started = time.monotonic()
        self._sampler = LoopingCall(self._sample)
        self._sampler.start(0.001)
        for i in range(BURST):
            yield scrapy.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/{i}", dont_filter=True)

    def parse(self, response):
        return

    def _sample(self):
        slot = self.crawler.engine.downloader.slots.get("127.0.0.1")
        if slot is not None:
            self.peak = max(self.peak, len(slot.transferring))

    def closed(self, reason):
        self._sampler.stop()
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self.started
        print(f"\n  reactor                     : {REACTOR.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]}")
        print(f"  download delay              : {DELAY}")
        print(f"  concurrency per domain      : {CONCURRENCY}")
        print(f"  requests sent               : {BURST}")
        print(f"  peak len(slot.transferring) : {self.peak}")
        print(f"  peak requests at the server : {_server_peak}")
        print(f"  elapsed                     : {elapsed:.2f}s "
              f"(at {CONCURRENCY} at a time: ~{BURST / CONCURRENCY * HOLD:.2f}s)\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    process = CrawlerProcess(settings={"TELNETCONSOLE_ENABLED": False})
    process.crawl(BurstSpider)
    process.start()
```

## Expected behaviour

No more than 2 requests in flight to the host at once, so 20 requests at 0.25 s each
take roughly 2.5 s.

## Actual behaviour

```
  reactor                     : AsyncioSelectorReactor
  download delay              : 0.0
  concurrency per domain      : 2
  requests sent               : 20
  peak len(slot.transferring) : 18          <- expected <= 2
  peak requests at the server : 18          <- expected <= 2
  elapsed                     : 0.54s       <- expected ~2.50s
```

Either a non-zero delay or a non-asyncio reactor gives the expected result, which is
what points at the cause:

```
$ DELAY=0.05 python mre.py
  peak len(slot.transferring) : 2
  peak requests at the server : 2
  elapsed                     : 2.63s

$ REACTOR=select python mre.py
  peak len(slot.transferring) : 2
  peak requests at the server : 2
  elapsed                     : 2.56s
```

The peak is 18 on almost every run, occasionally 19, depending on how many requests the
engine has fed before the first transfer registers.

## Diagnosis

`Downloader._process_queue`:

```python
while slot.queue and slot.free_transfer_slots() > 0:
    slot.lastseen = now
    request, queue_dfd = slot.queue.popleft()
    download_dfd = deferred_from_coro(
        self._wait_for_download(slot, request, queue_dfd)
    )
    ...
    # prevent burst if inter-request delays were configured
    if delay:
        self._process_queue(slot)
        break
```

`free_transfer_slots()` is `concurrency - len(slot.transferring)`, but
`slot.transferring.add(request)` happens inside `_download`. Under the asyncio reactor,
`deferred_from_coro` wraps the coroutine in an asyncio task, which doesn't start until
the loop yields. So `len(slot.transferring)` can't grow while this loop runs,
`free_transfer_slots()` returns the same value on every iteration, and the loop drains
the whole queue.

Two things hide it:

- **A delay.** The `if delay:` branch stops after one request and re-arms through
  `latercall`, so the count is up to date by the time the loop runs again.
- **A non-asyncio reactor.** There the coroutine runs straight away, up to its first
  real suspension, which is past the `transferring.add`, so the count is already current.

(In 2.18.0 the line is `_schedule_coro(...)`, which calls `loop.create_task` under
asyncio; same effect.)

## Possible fix

Counting a request as transferring when it is popped, rather than when its coroutine
starts, keeps `free_transfer_slots()` accurate inside the loop:

```diff
 request, queue_dfd = slot.queue.popleft()
+slot.transferring.add(request)
 download_dfd = deferred_from_coro(
```

`_download` already adds the request to the same set (a second add does nothing) and
removes it in its `finally`. 

When applying this in a fork, this gives:

| | slot peak | server peak | elapsed | responses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master, `delay 0` | 18 | 18 | 0.53 s | 20/20 |
| patched, `delay 0` | **2** | **2** | 2.56 s | 20/20 |
| patched, `delay 0.05` | 2 | 2 | 2.64 s | 20/20 |
| patched, Scrapy defaults (limit 8) | 8 | 8 | 1.28 s | 40/40 |


## Versions

```
Scrapy       : 2.19.0
Python       : 3.12.14
Twisted      : 26.4.0
lxml         : 6.1.3
Platform     : macOS 27.0 (arm64)
Reactor      : twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor
```

issue_title: Response data is not released after processing?
issue_body:
Hello,

code sample:
```
def start_requests(self):
    for url in url_list:
            yield scrapy.Request(url=url, headers = xxx, callback=self.parse, errback=None,dont_filter=False)

def parse(self, response):
    ...
    response.xpath('//*[@id="feed-main-list"]/li')
    ...
```
If we call selector related function like xpath(...), the response data will not be released after parsing of each url.

In scrapy/http/response/text.py, 
```
class TextResponse(Response):
...
    def selector(self):
        from scrapy.selector import Selector
        if self._cached_selector is None:
            self._cached_selector = Selector(self)
        return self._cached_selector

    def xpath(self, query, **kwargs):
        return self.selector.xpath(query, **kwargs)
```
It has the cyclic reference like response -> Selector -> response.
In my rough test, if i don't use self._cached_selector to keep Selector object, the memory usage will reduce from 6x% -> 4x%. 

So, am i right? or how to understand it?

issue_title: Request priority not guaranteed with the default scheduler configurations due to different queues (memory/disk) used.
issue_body:
**Description**

Request priority not guaranteed with the default scheduler configurations due to different queues (memory/disk) used.

**Reproduction of the issue**

```
$ scrapy shell -s JOBDIR=/tmp/scrapytmp -s LOG_UNSERIALIZABLE_REQUESTS=0
(MULTIPLE LINES OMITTED HERE)
In [1]: schdlr = scrapy.core.scheduler.Scheduler.from_crawler(crawler)                                                                                                                        

In [2]: schdlr.open(spider)                                                                                                                                                                   

In [3]: schdlr.enqueue_request(scrapy.Request('http://a.com/mqs-0-unserializable', meta={'foo': lambda: 'bar'}, priority=0))                                                                  
Out[3]: True

In [4]: schdlr.enqueue_request(scrapy.Request('http://a.com/dqs-100', priority=100))                                                                                                          
Out[4]: True

In [5]: schdlr.next_request()                                                                                                                                                                 
Out[5]: <GET http://a.com/mqs-0-unserializable>

In [6]: schdlr.next_request()                                                                                                                                                                 
Out[6]: <GET http://a.com/dqs-100>
```

Scrapy version involved: c72ab1d (the current HEAD).

**Expected behavior**

The request with higher priority shall have come out first.

**Cause of the issue**

The scheduler maintains two queues (memory / disk) and the memory queue always have a higher priority when generating the next request.
Related code: https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/blob/c72ab1d/scrapy/core/scheduler.py#L66

issue_title: Fix timezone handling in `FilesPipeline` stores
issue_body:
Found in https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/pull/8182#discussion_r4053447020

Various `FilesPipeline` stores produce the `last_modifed` value as the UNIX timestamp and some or all of them may do it incorrectly, depending on what are the values returned by S3 and GCS and what is in FTP `MDTM`. Their tests may also hide these problems and may need to be improved.

index 8e49f52e97f..c5f8ef9f940 100644
--- a/scrapy/pipelines/files.py
+++ b/scrapy/pipelines/files.py
@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@

 from contextlib import suppress
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
 from ftplib import FTP
 from io import BytesIO
 from pathlib import Path
@@ -202,7 +203,7 @@ def __init__(self, uri: str):
     def _onsuccess(boto_key: dict[str, Any]) -> StatInfo:
         checksum = boto_key["ETag"].strip('"')
         last_modified = boto_key["LastModified"]
-        modified_stamp = time.mktime(last_modified.timetuple())
+        modified_stamp = last_modified.timestamp()
         return {"checksum": checksum, "last_modified": modified_stamp}
 
     def stat_file(
@@ -326,7 +327,7 @@ def __init__(self, uri: str):
     def _onsuccess(blob: Any) -> StatInfo:
         if blob:
             checksum = base64.b64decode(blob.md5_hash).hex()
-            last_modified = time.mktime(blob.updated.timetuple())
+            last_modified = blob.updated.timestamp()
             return {"checksum": checksum, "last_modified": last_modified}
         return {}
 
@@ -420,7 +421,13 @@ def _stat_file(self, path: str) -> StatInfo:
                 if self.USE_ACTIVE_MODE:
                     ftp.set_pasv(False)
                 file_path = f"{self.basedir}/{path}"
-                last_modified = float(ftp.voidcmd(f"MDTM {file_path}")[4:].strip())
+                modified = ftp.voidcmd(f"MDTM {file_path}")[4:].strip()
+                time_format = "%Y%m%d%H%M%S.%f" if "." in modified else "%Y%m%d%H%M%S"
+                last_modified = (
+                    datetime.strptime(modified, time_format)
+                    .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+                    .timestamp()
+                )
                 m = hashlib.md5()  # noqa: S324
                 ftp.retrbinary(f"RETR {file_path}", m.update)
             return {"last_modified": last_modified, "checksum": m.hexdigest()}

--- a/docs/topics/media-pipeline.rst
+++ b/docs/topics/media-pipeline.rst
@@ -314,6 +314,28 @@ policy:
 
 For more information, see `canned ACLs`_ in the Amazon S3 Developer Guide.
 
+To send custom headers with the uploaded files, subclass ``S3FilesStore``
+with a different ``HEADERS`` class attribute, and point the ``s3`` scheme of
+your pipeline to it:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+    from scrapy.pipelines.files import FilesPipeline, S3FilesStore
+
+
+    class CustomS3FilesStore(S3FilesStore):
+        HEADERS = {
+            "Cache-Control": "max-age=172800",
+            "X-Amz-Storage-Class": "STANDARD_IA",
+        }
+
+
+    class CustomFilesPipeline(FilesPipeline):
+        STORE_SCHEMES = FilesPipeline.STORE_SCHEMES | {"s3": CustomS3FilesStore}
+
+Supported headers are those that the installed botocore version models for
+the `PutObject`_ operation; any other header raises :exc:`TypeError`.
+
 You can also use other S3-like storages. Storages like self-hosted `Minio`_ or
 `Zenko CloudServer`_. All you need to do is set the endpoint option in your
 Scrapy settings:

issue_title: Settings imports module for every component-dict key incl. None — ModuleNotFoundError on removed/disabled modules (2.17 regression)
issue_body:
### Describe the bug

Since Scrapy 2.17, `Settings.get_component_priority_dict_with_base()` normalizes **every** key of a component priority dictionary (`EXTENSIONS` / `SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES` / `DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES`) by calling `load_object()` on it — **including keys whose value is `None`** (i.e. components the user is explicitly disabling). On Scrapy ≤2.14, `None`-valued keys were not imported, so a stale reference to a module that no longer exists (e.g. a previously-default extension later removed from Scrapy) could live harmlessly in a user's `EXTENSIONS` override. On 2.17 the very same config aborts startup with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

`normalize_key()` only catches `(NameError, TypeError, ValueError)`, so the `ModuleNotFoundError`/`ImportError` raised by `importlib.import_module()` propagates and crashes the crawl in `_apply_settings` → `ExtensionManager.from_crawler`.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from scrapy.settings import Settings

s = Settings()
s.set("EXTENSIONS", {"nonexistent.module.Extension": None}, priority="cmdline")
s.get_component_priority_dict_with_base("EXTENSIONS")
# Scrapy <=2.14: OK (None-valued key not imported)
# Scrapy 2.17:   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nonexistent'
```

### Real-world case

A project that for years disabled the (since-removed) webservice with `'scrapy.webservice.WebService': None` fails to start on 2.17:

```
File ".../scrapy/extension.py", in _get_mwlist_from_settings
    settings.get_component_priority_dict_with_base("EXTENSIONS")
File ".../scrapy/settings/__init__.py", in get_component_priority_dict_with_base
    override = {normalize_key(k): v for k, v in (self[name] or {}).items()}
File ".../scrapy/settings/__init__.py", in normalize_key
    loaded_key = load_object(key)
...
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scrapy.webservice'
```

Because this surfaces inside a Deferred, in practice it looks like the spider *hangs* on download — it actually never starts.

### Expected behavior

A value of `None` means "disable this component"; importing the module of a disabled component is unnecessary, and an unimportable module under a `None` key should not abort settings resolution.

### Suggested fix

Broaden the exception guard in `normalize_key()` (`scrapy/settings/__init__.py`, currently around L366-369):

```python
def normalize_key(key):
    try:
        loaded_key = load_object(key)
    except Exception:                 # was: except (NameError, TypeError, ValueError):
        loaded_key = key
    ...
```

When the module can't be imported, `loaded_key` falls back to the raw key string; since the value is `None`, the entry is dropped by the subsequent `if v is not None` filter, so disabling keeps working.

Note: one cannot instead "skip normalizing `None`-valued keys" — normalization is exactly what makes a `None` override match the corresponding key in `<NAME>_BASE` and disable a default component. Skipping `None` keys would silently re-enable every default extension/middleware the user meant to turn off.

### Environment

- Scrapy version: 2.17.0 (also reproduces on current `master`, `scrapy/settings/__init__.py` ~L366-369)
- Python: 3.14.6
- OS: Linux

issue_title: [BUG] PromptBase.on_validate_error should explicitly enable markup
issue_body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

**Describe the bug**

I create a console with `Console(markup=False)` and then pass it to `Confirm.ask(..., console=console)`.  If the user doesn't pick a valid choice, they get an error that says `[prompt.invalid]Please enter Y or N`.

I think `PromptBase.on_validate_error()` should explicitly pass `markup=true` to `self.console.print(error)`.

**Platform**

Every platform, it's a logic bug.  (I'm on Ubuntu 25.10 with gnome-terminal, which doesn't matter.)

             value (str): String entered by user.
             error (InvalidResponse): Exception instance the initiated the error.
         """

+        self.console.print(error, markup=True)
 
     def pre_prompt(self) -> None:

issue_title: Add launch_edge() to the Browser addon?

isolated, proxy-configured instance of Chrome or Firefox via
`browser.start`, but has no equivalent for Microsoft Edge. Users who
don't have Chrome or Firefox installed -- e.g. Windows users, where
Edge is always pre-installed -- currently have no working option.

#### Proposal
Add launch_edge(), following the exact same pattern as launch_chrome()
and launch_firefox(), wired into the browser.start dispatcher. I have a
working implementation with tests ready to submit if this is welcome.

issue_title: Addon options are not shown in help

#### Problem Description

While troubleshooting #3377 I tried to see if an addon is loaded by inspecting options list. However `mitmproxy` processes `--options` flag without loadng the script.

#### Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1, Create `option_script.py`
```python
def load(l):

        "hardump", str, "", "HAR dump path.",
    )
```

2. Run `mitmdump -s option_script.py --options | grep hardump` to see there is no any`hardump` strings in output.
3. Run `mitmdump -s option_script.py` to see that addon is loaded.

issue_title: block_list implicitly lowercases attached filter expression
issue_body:
## Problem Description

I've been recently trying to add a `block_list` rule which implements "if request has header XYZ then return status code 500" behaviour. It didn't work as expected despite of the fact exactly the same filter expression did work in other built-in addons (e.g. `modify_headers`).

I started searching GH issues and stumbled upon #6329. It revealed that `|~hq X-Custom:\\sfoo|500` is effectively treated as `|~hq x-custom:\\sfoo|500` because of `.lower()` call [here](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/v11.0.2/mitmproxy/addons/blocklist.py#L27). I find this controversial because:

- even though HTTP header names should be treated as case-insensitive according to an RFC, header values certainly don't follow that rule
- filter expression are quite rich and current `block_list` behaviour makes certain implementations impossible, e.g. block request when its body contains `FOO`, but not `foo` or when `Cookie` header contains `BAR=1`, but not `bar=1`
- aforementioned ticket resulted in #6493 which globally turned `~u` filter into a case-insensitive regex. That change had far-reaching consequences - right now if you'd like to attach some logic to `/process/ME/please.html` requests, while leaving `/process/me/please.html` unaffected, it's simply not possible using built-in addons

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put the following in `~/.mitmproxy/config.yaml` file:
```yaml
block_list:
  - "|~hq X-Custom:\\sfoo|500"
modify_headers:
  - "|~hq X-Custom:\\sfoo|x-custom-matched|true"
  - "|~u /process/ME/please\\.html$|x-url-matched|true"
flow_detail: 2
```
2. Start `mitmdump` with: `mitmdump --mode reverse:https://httpbingo.org -p 8443` command
3. Request some content via `mitmdump` instance:

### `https://` + HTTP/1.1 + `X-Custom: foo` header

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: 500 + "x-custom-matched: true" response header
# Got: 200 + "x-custom-matched: true"
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl -k https://localhost:8443/headers -SsD - -o /dev/null -H "X-Custom: foo" --http1.1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: *
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
date: Mon, 06 Jan 2025 22:31:41 GMT
content-length: 535
server: Fly/d5165e6e2 (2024-12-18)
via: 1.1 fly.io
fly-request-id: 01JGYVXJ3W2ZQ5R0NZ61X7XJ77-arn
x-custom-matched: true
```

### `https://` + HTTP/2 + `X-Custom: foo` header

Everything's the same except HTTP/2. Headers got lowercased by `curl` which accidentally matched to that implicitly lowercased filter expression in `block_list`:

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: 200 w/o custom response header
# Got: 500 w/o response custom header
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl -k https://localhost:8443/headers -SsD - -o /dev/null -H "x-custom: foo" --http1.1
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Server: mitmproxy 11.0.2
content-length: 0
```

### `https://` + HTTP/1.1 + `x-custom: foo` header

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: 200 w/o custom response header
# Got: 500 w/o response custom header
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl -k https://localhost:8443/headers -SsD - -o /dev/null -H "x-custom: foo" --http1.1
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Server: mitmproxy 11.0.2
content-length: 0
```

### `http://` + HTTP/1.1 + `X-Custom: foo` header

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: 500 + "x-custom-matched: true" response header
# Got: 200 + "x-custom-matched: true"
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl http://localhost:8443/headers -SsD - -o /dev/null -H "X-Custom: foo" --http1.1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: *
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
date: Mon, 06 Jan 2025 22:41:49 GMT
content-length: 535
server: Fly/d5165e6e2 (2024-12-18)
via: 1.1 fly.io
fly-request-id: 01JGYWG3V3ASVBKB7VDRGNMD6H-arn
x-custom-matched: true
```

### `http://` + HTTP/2 + `X-Custom: foo` header

As per `mitmdump`'s log message h2c is not supported, so the result is exactly the same as via HTTP/1.1

```
HTTP/2 cleartext connections (h2c upgrade requests) are currently not supported.
```

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: 500 + "x-custom-matched: true" response header
# Got: 200 + "x-custom-matched: true"
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl http://localhost:8443/headers -SsD - -o /dev/null -H "X-Custom: foo" --http2
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: *
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
date: Mon, 06 Jan 2025 22:42:13 GMT
content-length: 535
server: Fly/d5165e6e2 (2024-12-18)
via: 1.1 fly.io
fly-request-id: 01JGYWGW4Q4T1C9B8S7JGVC93V-arn
x-custom-matched: true
```

### Case-insensitive `~u` example

```
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: "x-url-matched: true" header
# Got: "x-url-matched: true" header
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl -k https://localhost:8443/process/ME/please.html -SsD -
HTTP/2 404
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: *
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
x-content-type-options: nosniff
date: Mon, 06 Jan 2025 22:44:59 GMT
content-length: 19
server: Fly/d5165e6e2 (2024-12-18)
via: 2 fly.io
fly-request-id: 01JGYWNXMAXNK7WB1MZ1318106-arn
x-url-matched: true

404 page not found

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Expected: NO custom header
# Got: "x-url-matched: true" header
# -------------------------------------------------------------
$ curl -k https://localhost:8443/process/me/please.html -SsD -
HTTP/2 404
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: *
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
x-content-type-options: nosniff
date: Mon, 06 Jan 2025 22:45:05 GMT
content-length: 19
server: Fly/d5165e6e2 (2024-12-18)
via: 2 fly.io
fly-request-id: 01JGYWP39TM9DKFR5X6Q9K5AFV-arn
x-url-matched: true

404 page not found
```

## Expected state

1. `block_list` filter expressions must not be silently lowercased, but rather treated as-is
3. Don't treat `~u` as case-insensitive (or add an option to switch to case-**sensitive** matching)

## Noteworthy facts

1. A switch from HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2 results in a totally different response (`200` vs `500`)
2. A custom addon can be used as a fallback to circumvent these issues, but it sort of defeats the purpose of built-in addons
3. `mitmdump` output: https://gist.github.com/jwadolowski/c525d4b36d973b97cfb857414f1d7d78

## System Information

```
$ mitmproxy --version
Mitmproxy: 11.0.2 binary
Python:    3.12.7
OpenSSL:   OpenSSL 3.4.0 22 Oct 2024
Platform:  macOS-15.2-arm64-arm-64bit
```

PS. I've been using `mitmproxy` for years and find it extremely useful to debug HTTP flows.

+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -17,6 +17,8 @@
   ([#7385](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/pull/7385), @lups2000)
 - Add missing status codes
   ([#7455])(https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/pull/7455, @jwadolowski)
+- Remove filter expression lowercasing in block_list addon

+++ b/mitmproxy/addons/blocklist.py

issue_title: `CurvesAsSubmobjects` error messages contain hardcoded class names
issue_body:
The class `CurvesAsSubmobjects` throws two custom error messages for when it either has no submobjects or it has no submobjects with points:
https://github.com/ManimCommunity/manim/blob/cafc63919eb03d398d7038a8c82e591b12de8da5/manim/mobject/types/vectorized_mobject.py#L2858-L2874
These error messages contain a hardcodes class name, causing issues if `CurvesAsSubmobjects` is subclassed. This should be fixed.

This implementation was originally a response to a hardcoded class name in the `throw_error_if_no_points` method of `Mobject`, but that has since been made dynamic (#4927) so this override is now unnecessary. It's possible that the "no submobjects with points" case might need special handling in `CurvesAsSubmobjects`, but it should likely be based on the error message produced in `Mobject.throw_error_if_no_points`. Or perhaps `Mobject` needs a `throw_error_if_no_submobjects_with_points` method? Not sure, use your best judgment.

This issue is labeled "good first issue" and is intended for a human who wants to start contributing to the library, so AI-generated pull requests are discouraged. Say hi either here or on Discord if you are interested in familiarising yourself with the codebase, we're happy to provide pointers.

+from __future__ import annotations

+def test_camera_interpolate_angles(using_opengl_renderer):
+    # Literal -340-degree theta change and two positive gamma revolutions.
+    start_angles = np.array([350, 40, -10]) * DEGREES
+    target_angles = np.array([10, 65, 710]) * DEGREES
+    start = OpenGLCamera().set_euler_angles(*start_angles)
+    target = start.copy().set_euler_angles(*target_angles)
+    camera = start.copy()
+    reference = start.copy()
+    start_matrix = start.inverse_rotation_matrix.copy()
+    target_matrix = target.inverse_rotation_matrix.copy()
+
+    # Repeated and out-of-order samples must still use the fixed endpoints.
+    for alpha in (0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 0.5, 1):
+        expected = (1 - alpha) * start_angles + alpha * target_angles
+        assert camera.interpolate(start, target, alpha) is camera
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(camera.euler_angles, expected, atol=1e-12)
+        reference.set_euler_angles(*expected)
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(
+            camera.inverse_rotation_matrix,
+            reference.inverse_rotation_matrix,
+            atol=1e-12,
+        )
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(start.euler_angles, start_angles)
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(target.euler_angles, target_angles)
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(start.inverse_rotation_matrix, start_matrix)
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(target.inverse_rotation_matrix, target_matrix)
+

+    start = OpenGLCamera().set_euler_angles(0.2, 0.4, -0.1)
+    target = start.copy().set_euler_angles(0.7, 0.9, 0.3).move_to([1, 2, 0.5])
+    camera = start.copy()
+
+    def curved_path(start_points, target_points, alpha):
+        return (
+            (1 - alpha) * start_points
+            + alpha * target_points
+            + np.array([0, 0, np.sin(np.pi * alpha)])
+        )
+
+    camera.interpolate(start, target, 0.5, path_func=curved_path)
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(
+        camera.points, (start.points + target.points) / 2 + [0, 0, 1]
+    )
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(
+        camera.euler_angles, (start.euler_angles + target.euler_angles) / 2
+    )
+

+    start_angles = np.array([20, 40, -10]) * DEGREES

+    target_angles[0] -= 360 * DEGREES

+    )

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from manim import DEGREES, ThreeDScene, Transform, config, linear
+
+
+def test_set_camera_orientation(using_opengl_renderer):
+    scene = ThreeDScene()
+    scene.set_camera_orientation(
+        phi=70 * DEGREES, theta=-35 * DEGREES, zoom=0.72, frame_center=[1, 2, 0]
+    )
+    theta, phi, _ = scene.camera.euler_angles
+    assert phi == pytest.approx(70 * DEGREES)
+    assert theta == pytest.approx(-35 * DEGREES)
+    assert scene.camera.get_height() == pytest.approx(config.frame_height / 0.72)
+    assert scene.camera.frame_center == pytest.approx([1, 2, 0])
+
+
+def test_set_camera_orientation_zoom_is_absolute(using_opengl_renderer):
+    scene = ThreeDScene()
+    scene.set_camera_orientation(zoom=2)
+    scene.set_camera_orientation(zoom=2)
+    assert scene.camera.get_height() == pytest.approx(config.frame_height / 2)
+
+
+def test_set_camera_orientation_focal_distance_warns(using_opengl_renderer):
+    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="focal distance"):
+        ThreeDScene().set_camera_orientation(focal_distance=5)
+
+
+def _capture_camera_animation(scene, monkeypatch, **kwargs):
+    # Exercise move_camera's real target construction without a render loop.
+    play = Mock()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(scene, "play", play)
+    scene.move_camera(**kwargs, rate_func=linear)
+    play.assert_called_once()
+    (animation,), play_kwargs = play.call_args
+    assert isinstance(animation, Transform)
+    assert animation.mobject is scene.camera
+    animation.rate_func = play_kwargs["rate_func"]
+    return animation
+
+
+def test_move_camera_interpolates_and_preserves_omitted_settings(
+    using_opengl_renderer, monkeypatch
+):
+    scene = ThreeDScene()
+    start_angles = np.array([20, 40, -10]) * DEGREES
+    target_angles = np.array([-35, 65, 15]) * DEGREES
+    start_center = np.array([-1, 0, 0.3])
+    target_center = np.array([1, 0.5, 0.2])
+    scene.set_camera_orientation(
+        theta=start_angles[0],
+        phi=start_angles[1],
+        gamma=start_angles[2],
+        zoom=0.72,
+        frame_center=start_center,
+    )
+    start_height = scene.camera.get_height()
+    target_zoom = 1.5
+    target_height = config.frame_height / target_zoom
+    aspect_ratio = scene.camera.get_width() / start_height
+    animation = _capture_camera_animation(
+        scene,
+        monkeypatch,
+        theta=target_angles[0],
+        phi=target_angles[1],
+        gamma=target_angles[2],
+        zoom=target_zoom,
+        frame_center=target_center,
+    )
+    animation.begin()
+
+    for alpha in (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1):
+        animation.interpolate(alpha)
+        expected_angles = (1 - alpha) * start_angles + alpha * target_angles
+        expected_center = (1 - alpha) * start_center + alpha * target_center
+        # Preserve OpenGL's frame-height interpolation, not linear zoom.
+        expected_height = (1 - alpha) * start_height + alpha * target_height
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(
+            scene.camera.euler_angles, expected_angles, atol=1e-12
+        )
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(
+            scene.camera.get_center(), expected_center, atol=1e-12
+        )
+        assert scene.camera.get_height() == pytest.approx(expected_height)
+        assert scene.camera.get_width() == pytest.approx(aspect_ratio * expected_height)
+
+    animation.finish()
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(scene.camera.euler_angles, target_angles)
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(scene.camera.get_center(), target_center)
+    assert scene.camera.get_height() == pytest.approx(target_height)
+
+    # Reuse the scene to check a partial update without another OpenGL context.
+    partial_angles = target_angles.copy()
+    partial_angles[1] += 15 * DEGREES
+    animation = _capture_camera_animation(scene, monkeypatch, phi=partial_angles[1])
+    animation.begin()
+    for alpha in (0.5, 1):
+        animation.interpolate(alpha)
+        expected_angles = (1 - alpha) * target_angles + alpha * partial_angles
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(scene.camera.euler_angles, expected_angles)
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(scene.camera.get_center(), target_center)
+        assert scene.camera.get_height() == pytest.approx(target_height)
+        assert scene.camera.get_width() == pytest.approx(aspect_ratio * target_height)
+    animation.finish()
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(scene.camera.euler_angles, partial_angles)

issue_title: Opaque white stroke is drawn on shapes with `stroke="none"`
issue_body:
## Description of bug / unexpected behavior Currently, if a shape with `stroke="none"` has a stroke width that is not zero, an opaque white outline of that width is drawn. To show it, I attached an image below, it is the black knight from the Lichess "cburnett" chess pieces, as used by [manim-chess](https://github.com/swoyer2/manim_chess). The knight's white mane stripe is a `stroke="none"` path inside a ``. 1. The SVG as rendered by ImageMagick, as designed. The stripe sits inside the knight's black outline. 2. Manim 0.21.0. The stripe gets a white outline, 1.5 wide, so it covers the black edge and pokes out past the bottom of the knight. 3. The same as 2, with only the stripe's stroke width set to 0. It now matches 1. 4. The same as 3, with the black outline's width also scaled to the piece. This is a separate, known behaviour (stroke widths don't scale with the SVG, see #4836) and isn't part of this report. ## Expected behavior A shape with `stroke="none"` should have no outline, as in 1 and 3. ## How to reproduce the issue
Code for reproducing the problem `stroke_none.svg`: ```svg ``` ```py from manim import * class StrokeNone(Scene): def construct(self): self.camera.background_color = GREY svg = SVGMobject("stroke_none.svg", height=6) self.add(svg) for i, sub in enumerate(svg.submobjects): print(i, "stroke", sub.get_stroke_color().to_hex(), "width", sub.get_stroke_width(), "opacity", sub.get_stroke_opacity()) ``` `manim -ql -s -v DEBUG repro.py StrokeNone`
## Additional media files
Images/GIFs
## Logs
Terminal output ``` Manim Community v0.21.0 0 stroke #000000 width 4.0 opacity 1.0 1 stroke #FFFFFF width 4.0 opacity 1.0 [09/27/26 01:50:47] INFO scene_file_writer.py:1103 File ready at '/tmp/claude-1000/manim_issue/media/images/repro/StrokeNone_ManimCE_v0.21.0.png' INFO Rendered StrokeNone scene.py:290 Played 0 animations ```
## System specifications
System Details - OS: Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition) - RAM: 16.0 GiB - Python version: 3.14.7 - Installed modules (provide output from `pip list`): ``` Package Version ----------------- ------- audioop-lts 0.2.2 av 18.1.0 beautifulsoup4 4.15.0 chess 1.11.2 click 8.5.0 cloup 4.0.0 decorator 5.3.1 glcontext 3.0.0 isosurfaces 0.1.2 manim 0.21.0 manim-chess 0.0.38 manimpango 0.6.1 mapbox-earcut 2.1.0 markdown-it-py 4.2.0 mdurl 0.1.2 moderngl 5.12.0 moderngl-window 3.1.1 networkx 3.7 numpy 2.5.3 pillow 12.3.0 pycairo 1.29.1 pydub 0.25.1 pyglet 2.1.16 pyglm 2.8.3 pygments 2.21.0 rich 15.0.0 scipy 1.18.1 screeninfo 0.8.1 skia-pathops 0.9.2 soupsieve 2.9.2 srt 3.5.3 svgelements 1.9.6 tqdm 4.70.1 typing-extensions 4.16.0 watchdog 6.0.0 ```
LaTeX details + Not installed (not needed to reproduce)
## Additional comments The cause is in `SVGMobject.apply_style_to_mobject`: ```py mob.set_style( stroke_width=shape.stroke_width, stroke_color=shape.stroke.hexrgb, stroke_opacity=shape.stroke.opacity, ... ) ``` svgelements parses `stroke="none"` as a `Color` whose `hexrgb` and `opacity` are both `None`, while `stroke_width` is still the inherited value. `set_style` ignores `None` arguments, so the mobject keeps the default stroke colour (white, fully opaque) at that width. `fill="none"` doesn't have this problem because the default fill opacity is 0. A possible fix, which produces the image below: ```py mob.set_style(...) # unchanged if shape.stroke is None or shape.stroke.value is None: mob.set_stroke(width=0) ```

@@ -375,8 +375,9 @@ def apply_style_to_mobject(mob: VMobject, shape: se.GraphicObject) -> VMobject:

             The parsed SVG element.

+        # stroke="none" still inherits a stroke-width, but has no color to draw it with

             stroke_color=shape.stroke.hexrgb,

issue_title: `redirections` parameter of `deprecated_params` decorator not working
issue_body:
## Description of bug / unexpected behavior
When using the `redirections` parameter of the `deprecated_params` decorator, a lot of function usages aren't allowed even though I would expect them to.

Here for example, I renamed the `a,b,c` parameters to `x,y,z`.
```py
from manim.utils.deprecation import deprecated_params

@deprecated_params(redirections=[("a", "x"), ("b", "y"), ("c", "z")])
def foo(x: int, /, y: int, *, z: int) -> None:
    print(x, y, z)
```
So I would expect all the following calls to be valid, albeit some should issue a warnings:
```py
foo(1, 2, z=3)  # no warning
foo(1, y=2, z=3)  # no warning
foo(1, b=2, z=3)  # warning for 'b'
foo(1, 2, c=3)  # warning for 'c'
foo(1, y=2, c=3)  # warning for 'c'
foo(1, b=2, c=3)  # warning for 'b' and 'c'
```

But here are the actual results:
```py
foo(1, 2, z=3)
foo(1, y=2, z=3)
foo(1, b=2, z=3)  # TypeError: missing a required argument: 'y'
foo(1, 2, c=3)  # TypeError: missing a required keyword-only argument: 'z'
foo(1, y=2, c=3)  # TypeError: missing a required argument: 'z'
foo(1, b=2, c=3)  # TypeError: missing a required argument: 'y'
```

issue_title: Changing cap style of Mobject to ROUND is influencing Write animations behavior
issue_body:
## Description of bug / unexpected behavior
When I change the cap style of an Mobject (a line, in my case) using either the parameter `cap_style=CapStyleType.ROUND` or the method `.set_cap_style(CapStyleType.ROUND)` , subsequent Write() animations of MathTex equations appear with dots on the screen. Even though the MathTex object has no direct influence on the Mobject whose cap style was changed.

@nikolajmunk guesses that the points show up because round linestyle (by design) also applies a stroke to paths of length 0, while the other choices don't. That means we're suddenly seeing a stroke show up out of nowhere when the animation starts, even when it's at its beginning size of length 0.


## Expected behavior
The expectation is that changing the cap style of a Mobject will not affect other objects.


## How to reproduce the issue
This is a simple and clean version of the problem. As we can see, although the second equation is identical to the first, because it was instantiated after the line specifying `CapStyleType.ROUND`, dots appear on the screen when using the `Write` animation.

<details><summary>Code for reproducing the problem</summary>

```py
def construct(self):
    eq1 = MathTex(r"f(x)=ax^2+bx+c").scale(2)
    line = Line(cap_style=CapStyleType.ROUND)
    eq2 = MathTex(r"f(x)=ax^2+bx+c").scale(2)
    VGroup(eq1, line, eq2).arrange(DOWN, buff=1)

    self.play(Write(eq1, run_time=2))
    self.play(Create(line))
    self.play(Write(eq2, run_time=2))
    self.wait()
```

</details>

issue_title: LaggedStartMap(Write, group) raises TypeError in 0.21.0
issue_body:
## Description of bug / unexpected behavior

`LaggedStartMap` with a single-argument animation like `Write` fails. It seems each submobject is
unpacked into its own children instead of being passed as one argument. This worked in the version
I used before upgrading to 0.21.0.

In `LaggedStartMap.__init__` the default `arg_creator` returns the submobject itself, and the
animation is then built with `*args`:

```python
def identity(mob: Mobject) -> Mobject:
    return mob
...
animations = [animation_class(*args, **anim_kwargs) for args in args_list]
```

`Mobject` is iterable over its submobjects, so `*args` spreads a `Text` into its glyphs. `Write`
then gets one argument per glyph.

## Expected behavior

One animation per submobject, i.e. the same as `LaggedStart(*[Write(m) for m in group])`.

## How to reproduce the issue

<details><summary>Code for reproducing the problem</summary>

```py
from manim import *


class LaggedStartMapBug(Scene):
    def construct(self):

issue_title: MathTypst grouping can change math styling and spacing
issue_body:
## Description

The `{{ ... }}` shorthand in `MathTypst` can change the typesetting of the grouped expression instead of only adding selection metadata.

For example, grouping an integral changes it from display to inline sizing. In `dif x`, the grouped `x` is rendered as upright text rather than an italic math variable, with extra spacing between `d` and `x`.

## Expected behavior

The grouped and ungrouped expressions should have identical geometry and math styling; the group should only make the expression available through `select()`.

## Reproducer

```py
from manim import *


class TypstGrouping(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        plain = MathTypst(
            r"integral_0^infinity e^(-x^2) dif x",
            font_size=60,
        )
        grouped = MathTypst(
            r"{{ integral_0^infinity e^(-x^2) dif x : integral }}",
            font_size=60,
        )
        grouped.select("integral").set_color(BLUE)

        self.add(VGroup(plain, grouped).arrange(DOWN))
```

This appears to come from the injected helper placing the group body in `#box(body)`, which does not preserve the surrounding math context:

```typst
#let manimgrp(lbl, body) = [#box(body) #label(lbl)]
```

Observed with Manim v0.21.0 and Typst 0.14.0.

issue_title: Crash: ValueError: Unknown check type '' for sites without checkType in data.json
issue_body:
## Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting a bug in Maigret functionality
- [x] I've checked for similar bug reports including closed ones
- [x] I've checked for pull requests that attempt to fix this bug

## Description

Maigret version info:
```
maigret 0.6.6
Socid-extractor:  0.1.1
Aiohttp:  3.13.5
Requests:  2.34.2
Python:  3.12.0
```
OS: Linux x86_64 (Debian-based VPS)

How to reproduce:
```bash
maigret jak2k --site sr.ht
```
or any full scan (`--all-sites`) that includes one of the affected sites.

The scan crashes with:
```
ValueError: Unknown check type '' for site 'sr.ht'
```

### Root cause

Some entries in `data.json` have neither a `checkType` field nor an `engine`. For those, `MaigretSite.check_type` keeps its class default `""` (see `maigret/sites.py`), and `process_site_result()` in `maigret/checking.py` falls through to the final `else` branch and raises:

```python
raise ValueError(f"Unknown check type '{check_type}' for site '{site.name}'")
```

Currently 3686 of 6206 entries in `data.json` lack `checkType`, but almost all of them use an engine that supplies `check_type` at runtime, so they work fine. The crash only happens for entries with **neither** `checkType` **nor** an engine. Affected sites I've confirmed in the current DB:

- `cs.cmu.edu`
- `eggplant.place`
- `neodb.social`
- `sr.ht`
- `taittsuu.com`
- `tilde.club`

All six are simple profile-URL sites (`url` like `https://sr.ht/~{username}`) with no `urlProbe` and no presence strings, so a `status_code` check against the profile URL is the natural behavior.

### Proposed fix

In `MaigretSite.__init__`, normalize an empty `check_type` to `"status_code"` (without adding it to `stated_fields`, so entries that use an engine still get the engine's `check_type` with the existing precedence logic). I'm happy to open a PR with the fix + a regression test.

+
         if (self.alexa_rank is None) or (self.alexa_rank == 0):

issue_title: Non-UTF-8 stdout still crashes the verbose scan and the --ai spinner
issue_body:
#3050 guards the two startup banners against a stdout that cannot encode them. The same class of crash lives in two more places, and one of them is worse than the banner because it fires after the work is already done.

Both reproduce in a child process whose stdout really is cp1252, the default ANSI codepage on a stock Windows install:

```
ai spinner frame: CRASH UnicodeEncodeError
checking arrow:   CRASH UnicodeEncodeError
```

### `checking.py`, the `→` in URL mutation messages

Lines 1843, 1847, 1855 and 1895 build messages like `f"{site.name}: {mut_url} → status={status_code}, empty body"`. They travel `notify` -> `query_notify.enrich` -> `_colored_print` -> a bare `print()`, on the main thread. U+2192 is not in cp1252, so in verbose mode the first mutation message kills the scan in the middle of a run, with the sites already checked and no report written.

This is the one worth fixing first. It is behind `--verbose`, so it is rarer than the banner, but it costs the user a completed run rather than a startup.

### `ai.py`, the spinner frames

`_Spinner.FRAMES` on line 37 is braille, U+280B and friends. It writes to `sys.stderr` from a daemon thread, so the failure is milder: the thread dies with an `Exception in thread` traceback, the spinner disappears, and the process carries on. Only reachable with `--ai`.

### Note for whoever picks this up

`_print_encodable` from #3050 is the obvious tool for the `checking.py` side, but it wraps `print` and the spinner writes to `sys.stderr` directly, so the spinner needs either its own guard or a helper that takes a stream.

Worth checking one thing while in there. colorama's `AnsiToWin32.write_and_convert` writes the plain-text runs between ANSI codes one segment at a time, so on Windows part of a colored line reaches the stream before the error is raised, and a guard that retries the whole string prints the beginning twice:

```
raised: UnicodeEncodeError
bytes already written before the raise: b'['
```

Not a crash, just a cosmetic wart, and it applies to the banner guard in #3050 too. Encoding the text up front instead of catching the failed write would sidestep it.
code_patch:
diff --git a/maigret/ai.py b/maigret/ai.py
index cc48562ed..534b9656e 100644
--- a/maigret/ai.py
+++ b/maigret/ai.py
@@ -31,15 +31,34 @@ def resolve_api_key(settings) -> str | None:
     return os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
 
 
+def _frames_for(stream, frames, fallback):
+    """Pick a frame set the stream can actually render.
+
+    The braille frames are not in cp1252, the ANSI codepage of a stock Windows
+    install, so writing one raised UnicodeEncodeError inside the spinner's
+    daemon thread: the thread died with a traceback over the output and the
+    animation stopped for the rest of the run. Encoding with replacement would
+    only leave a row of '?' spinning, so fall back to frames that carry.
+    """
+    encoding = getattr(stream, "encoding", None) or "ascii"
+    try:
+        "".join(frames).encode(encoding)
+    except (UnicodeEncodeError, LookupError):
+        return fallback
+    return frames
+
+
 class _Spinner:
     """Simple animated spinner for terminal output."""
 
     FRAMES = ["⠋", "⠙", "⠹", "⠸", "⠼", "⠴", "⠦", "⠧", "⠇", "⠏"]
+    ASCII_FRAMES = ["|", "/", "-", "\\"]
 
     def __init__(self, text=""):
         self.text = text
         self._stop = threading.Event()
         self._thread = None
+        self._frames = _frames_for(sys.stderr, self.FRAMES, self.ASCII_FRAMES)
 
     def start(self):
         self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._spin, daemon=True)
@@ -48,7 +67,7 @@ def start(self):
     def _spin(self):
         i = 0
         while not self._stop.is_set():
-            frame = self.FRAMES[i % len(self.FRAMES)]
+            frame = self._frames[i % len(self._frames)]
             sys.stderr.write(f"\r{frame} {self.text}")
             sys.stderr.flush()
             i += 1

@@ -134,7 +134,7 @@ def warning(self, message, symbol="-", advice=None):

             # Bold + yellow for the count line; turn off bold for the advice

-            print(
+            _print_encodable(
                 Style.BRIGHT + Fore.YELLOW + msg
                 + Style.NORMAL + ". " + advice
                 + Style.RESET_ALL
@@ -142,7 +142,7 @@ def warning(self, message, symbol="-", advice=None):
         elif advice:
             # No-colour mode: dot separator is enough to distinguish the
             # parts, no ANSI codes leak into the output.
-            print(f"{msg}. {advice}")
+            _print_encodable(f"{msg}. {advice}")
         else:
             self._colored_print(Fore.YELLOW, msg)
 
@@ -249,7 +249,7 @@ def update(self, result, is_similar=False):
 
         if notify:
             sys.stdout.write("\x1b[1K\r")
-            print(notify)
+            _print_encodable(notify)
 
         return notify
 
@@ -281,6 +281,12 @@ def _print_encodable(text: str) -> None:
     the character sits in that branch too. PYTHONIOENCODING cannot rescue
     the PyInstaller build, which ignores PYTHON* environment variables.
 
+    Every line this module writes goes through here for the same reason.
+    A run reaches text the codepage cannot hold in two ordinary ways: the
+    --enrich notifications built in checking.py carry U+2192, and extracted
+    profile fields carry whatever script the page was written in. Both
+    arrive mid-scan, so the crash discarded work already done.
+
     Catching the write rather than reconfiguring the stream is deliberate:
     colorama's init() replaces sys.stdout with a wrapper that has no
     reconfigure(), so a stream-level fix would depend on running first.

diff --git a/tests/test_ai.py b/tests/test_ai.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..08a661545
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+"""Tests for maigret.ai terminal output."""
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+def _run_probe(tmp_path, name, lines, encoding):
+    """Run a probe in a child process whose streams really use `encoding`.
+
+    Forcing the encoding rather than mocking the failure is deliberate: this then
+    fails on any machine if the guard goes, the same way the banner test does.
+    """
+    probe = tmp_path / name
+    probe.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env["PYTHONIOENCODING"] = encoding

+        [sys.executable, str(probe)],
+        capture_output=True,
+        encoding=encoding,

+        cwd=str(tmp_path),
+    )

+def test_spinner_renders_on_a_stderr_that_cannot_encode_braille(tmp_path):
+    """The spinner frames are braille, which cp1252 -- the ANSI codepage of a
+    stock Windows install -- cannot encode. Writing one raised UnicodeEncodeError
+    inside the spinner's daemon thread: the thread died with a traceback printed
+    over the output, and the animation stopped for the rest of the run.
+    """
+    result = _run_probe(
+        tmp_path,
+        "spinner_probe.py",
+        [
+            "import sys, time",
+            "from maigret.ai import _Spinner",
+            "",
+            "spinner = _Spinner('probe')",
+            "spinner.start()",
+            "time.sleep(0.3)",
+            "spinner.stop()",
+            "sys.stdout.write('FRAMES=' + ''.join(spinner._frames) + chr(10))",
+            "sys.stdout.write('STILL_RUNNING=' + str(spinner._thread.is_alive()) + chr(10))",
+            "sys.stdout.write('REACHED_END' + chr(10))",

+    # The daemon thread swallows nothing: an encode failure surfaces as a
+    # traceback on stderr and leaves the spinner dead for the rest of the run.
+    assert "UnicodeEncodeError" not in result.stderr, f"stderr={result.stderr!r}"
+    assert "Exception in thread" not in result.stderr, f"stderr={result.stderr!r}"

issue_title: Graph and Neo4j reports crash on non-string extracted values
issue_body:
`-G/--graph` and `--neo4j` crash with `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith'` whenever an extracted identity field holds something that isn't a string.

`MaigretGraph.add_node` in `maigret/report.py:186` does this:

```python
if key in SUPPORTED_IDS:
    params = dict(self.username_params)
elif value.startswith('http'):
    params = dict(self.site_params)
```

`process_ids` feeds it `norm_v` straight from `ids_data`, and socid_extractor does not coerce values to strings. Its `extract()` ends with `{a: html_module.unescape(b) if isinstance(b, str) else b for a, b in values.items() if b or type(b) == bool}`, so ints, bools, lists and dicts from JSON schemes pass through untouched. The key filter above only drops `_count`, `is_`, `_at` and `image`, so a plain numeric field like `uid` walks right into `add_node`.

Reproduction, straight through the public entry point:

```python
from maigret.report import save_graph_report
from maigret.result import MaigretCheckResult, MaigretCheckStatus
from maigret.sites import MaigretDatabase

st = MaigretCheckResult(
    'user', 'ExampleSite', 'https://example.com/user',
    MaigretCheckStatus.CLAIMED,
    ids_data={'uid': 4242, 'name': 'John'},
)
results = [('user', 'username', {'ExampleSite': {'status': st, 'url_user': 'https://example.com/user'}})]
save_graph_report('/tmp/g.html', results, MaigretDatabase())
```

```
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith'
```

Both `save_graph_report` and `save_neo4j_report` go through `_build_maigret_graph`, so one guard in `add_node` covers both.

This is the same bug #3039 fixes for the console tree, in a second place. The idiom the codebase already uses for it is `isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith(...)`, see `report.py:270`. The fix wants a regression test that builds a graph from `ids_data` with a numeric field.

issue_title: extract_ids_from_page() re-adds a rejected bare 'username' value via SUPPORTED_IDS (same class as #2907)
issue_body:
`extract_ids_from_page()` in `maigret/maigret.py` has the same underlying bug that #2907 just fixed in `checking.py::parse_usernames()` — a bare `username` key extracted by socid_extractor bypasses the `is_plausible_username()` guard because `"username"` is itself in `SUPPORTED_IDS`:

```python
for k, v in info.items():
    if k in SUPPORTED_IDS:        # "username" is in SUPPORTED_IDS
        results[v] = k            # added here, unvalidated

for username in extract_usernames(info, logger):   # separate, validating pass
    results[username] = 'username'
```

The first loop is unconditional and runs before/independent of `extract_usernames()`. If socid_extractor returns a URL or email under a bare `username` key, `results[v] = k` stores it straight away — `extract_usernames()` rejecting the same value in its own pass doesn't remove what the first loop already added, since the two loops key the dict differently and neither loop knows about the other's decisions.

Repro:

```python
>>> info = {'username': 'https://instagram.com/zuck'}
>>> results = {}
>>> for k, v in info.items():
...     if k in SUPPORTED_IDS:
...         results[v] = k
>>> results
{'https://instagram.com/zuck': 'username'}
```

This matters because `extract_ids_from_page()` feeds directly into the initial username list for a scan:

```python
if args.parse_url:
    extracted_ids = extract_ids_from_page(args.parse_url, logger, timeout=args.timeout)
    usernames.update(extracted_ids)
```

So `maigret --parse-url <page-with-a-bare-username-field-that-is-a-URL>` reproduces the exact "wrong username" false-error cascade from #1403 that #2907 closed for the `checking.py` path — just via `--parse-url` instead of the recursive-search / enrich path.

**Suggested fix:** same shape as #2907 — don't let the `SUPPORTED_IDS` loop re-add a key that `extract_usernames()` already owns (i.e. skip keys containing `"username"` in the `SUPPORTED_IDS` loop, or run `extract_usernames()` first and only fill in `SUPPORTED_IDS` keys not already claimed).

No coverage gap fix included here — `tests/test_extractors.py::test_extract_ids_from_page_username_contract` mocks `extract` to return `{}`, so this path currently has no test exercising the real bug.

index 7604dda38..eb410248b 100755
--- a/maigret/maigret.py
+++ b/maigret/maigret.py
@@ -84,8 +84,9 @@ def extract_ids_from_page(url, logger, timeout=5) -> dict:
         else:
             print(get_dict_ascii_tree(info.items(), new_line=False), ' ')
         for k, v in info.items():
-
-            if k in SUPPORTED_IDS:
+            # keys containing "username" are owned by extract_usernames() below,
+            # which validates them; adding them here would bypass that check
+            if "username" not in k and k in SUPPORTED_IDS:
                 results[v] = k
 
         for username in extract_usernames(info, logger):

issue_title: Replace silent CheckerMock fallback for Tor/I2P/DNS with explicit skip status
issue_body:
## Problem

When the user does not pass `--tor-proxy` (or `--i2p-proxy`, or `--with-domains`), the corresponding checker is assigned a `CheckerMock` (`maigret/checking.py:557`) whose `check()` returns `('', 0, None)`. Every `.onion` / `.i2p` / domain entry in the database is then dispatched to that mock at `maigret/checking.py:845–847` via `options["checkers"][site.protocol]`.

A `status_code` of `0` is interpreted by `_make_request` at `maigret/checking.py:158` as `CheckError("Connection lost")`. The end-user sees a "Connection lost" error for every `.onion` site instead of an honest "skipped because no Tor gateway is configured" signal.

This is misleading in three ways:

- The site is not actually unreachable — it was never tried.
- `--print-errors` is polluted with fake "Connection lost" entries (3 sites today: `HiddenAnswers`, `DarkNet Trust`, `i2pforum`).
- Real connection-lost errors on clearweb sites become harder to spot.

## Proposed fix

Either:

- **(a)** extend `MaigretCheckStatus` (or reuse the existing `ILLEGAL`) and short-circuit dispatch when `site.protocol in ("tor", "i2p")` and the corresponding proxy is missing, returning an explicit `SKIPPED — no Tor gateway configured` status; or
- **(b)** instantiate the proxied checker lazily, only after the dispatcher confirms a site needs it, and skip the site cleanly otherwise.

## Acceptance

- Running `maigret <user>` without `--tor-proxy` produces no "Connection lost" entries for `.onion` sites.
- The CLI and JSON report visibly mark `.onion` sites as skipped, with a one-line explanation.
- A regression test in `tests/test_checking.py` (new) verifies the dispatch path.

## Code refs

- `maigret/checking.py:557` (`CheckerMock` definition)
- `maigret/checking.py:1105–1122` (the three bare `# TODO` comments above the mock fallbacks)
- `maigret/checking.py:158` (where `status_code=0` becomes "Connection lost")
- `maigret/checking.py:845–847` (dispatch by `site.protocol`)

## Related

- #544 (Tor/proxy documentation). The Tor-and-proxies docs page currently says ".onion sites are silently skipped", which is also inaccurate — merging this fix lets us tighten that wording.
- Two of the three onion entries in `data.json` are also rotten today (`DarkNet Trust` uses a v2 onion address that Tor deprecated in October 2021); cleaning that up is a separate concern but is part of the same audit.

issue_title: CSV and XMind reports silently drop the 'reason' of a failed check
issue_body:
## Problem

Both `generate_csv_report` and `design_xmind_sheet` discard the per-site error context when a result has no `status`:

- **CSV** (`maigret/report.py:588`): writes the literal string `'Unknown'` in the `exists` column. The consumer cannot distinguish "site was skipped because of protocol mismatch" from "site timed out" from "site returned a 403".
- **XMind** (`maigret/report.py:690`): silently filters the site out entirely (`if not result_status or result_status.status != CLAIMED: continue`).

This makes CSV/XMind exports much less useful than HTML / JSON, where the error message survives.

## Proposed fix

- Add an `error_reason` column (or reuse `http_status` + `check_error`) to the CSV header and write `result.error.context if result.error else 'Unknown'`.
- For XMind, emit a non-CLAIMED branch with the error reason as the topic title, similar to how the HTML report does it.

## Code refs

- `maigret/report.py:582–601` (CSV)
- `maigret/report.py:673–705` (XMind)
- `maigret/errors.py` (`CheckError` type)

issue_title: Test coverage gaps marked '# TODO: tests'
issue_body:
## Problem

Tracking issue for four code paths the original author flagged as untested. None of them are tested by `tests/` today. Each is independent and can be picked up separately.

## Untested paths

- **`maigret/checking.py:204`** — `ClientSession(..., cookie_jar=...)` path. Needs a unit test that the cookie jar passed to `SimpleAiohttpChecker.check` is actually used on the outgoing request. Trivial with `aioresponses`.
- **`maigret/executors.py:113`** — `increment_progress` switches between sync- and async-callable `progress_func`s; both branches need separate tests.
- **`maigret/executors.py:123`** — `stop_progress`, same sync/async-branch coverage.
- **`maigret/maigret.py:857`** — the recursive ID-extraction branch (`if recursive_search_enabled: extract_ids_from_results(...)`) has no coverage. Should be paired with the `extract_ids_from_results` work.

## Acceptance

- Each of the four lines is covered by at least one test in `tests/`.
- `make test` coverage report no longer shows these as uncovered.

+def _capture_clientsession(monkeypatch):

+    assert on the kwargs it received (cookie_jar in particular) without
+    opening any sockets. Mirrors the _capture_tcpconnector pattern above."""
+    from maigret import checking
+    captured = []
+
+    class _DummySession:
+        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            captured.append(kwargs)
+
+        async def __aenter__(self):
+            return self
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
+            return False
+
+        async def close(self):
+            pass
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(checking, 'ClientSession', _DummySession)
+    return captured
+

+    A sentinel object stands in for the real aiohttp.CookieJar: check() only
+    does `self.cookie_jar if self.cookie_jar else None`, so any truthy object
+    proves the forwarding. Avoiding CookieJar() also sidesteps its event-loop
